clue.text: Scrapheap prepared to receive European bureaucratic procedure

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take another piece in among them
the scrapheap is worked over and made ready afresh, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Junk dealers are made to accept some Brussels red tape before they can operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' signals an anagram of SCRAPHEAP, and 'to receive' says that anagram takes E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is slang for a tedious exchange of forms and documents, i.e. red tape.

clue.text: Eager with weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Someone keen to fight, holding a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm can mean enthusiastic or ardent, as in a warm welcome or warm support.

clue.text: Not wanted in university, book found in study returned

indicators.note: the study holding the book is turned round and read backwards
the book is placed inside the study

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
VOL is short for volume, a book

explanation.surface: A rejected student at university, with a book located back in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places the book inside the study, and 'returned' turns that whole combination round, giving NLOVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unloved is not cared for, so not wanted by anyone.

clue.text: Nastiness of Shakespeare twice shrugging off wife

indicators.note: the abbreviation for wife is cast off from the doubled name
the name is written two times over

parts.note: Will is William Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: The Bard's malice, shown twice, as he shook off his wife Anne Hathaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives WILLWILL and 'shrugging off' removes the first W.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or malice, a synonym for nastiness.

clue.text: Drink? Cheers! (Hiss?)

parts.note: to buck someone up is to cheer them, so bucks means cheers
fizz is a hissing sound, as from a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A toast with a drink, followed by a hiss as it is poured.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKS FIZZ is champagne mixed with orange juice; it was also a British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck's fizz is a cocktail of sparkling wine and orange juice, so an example of a drink.

clue.text: Distinctive theory probes meaning of green device

indicators.note: the theory pushes into the middle of the green signal

parts.note: a green traffic light means go
an ism is a distinctive doctrine or theory

explanation.surface: An ideology investigating what a green gadget is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is an informal word for a gadget, a small mechanical contrivance.

clue.text: Cotton material, turned and shortened, is shrinking

indicators.note: its final letter is cut off
the fabric's name is read from back to front

parts.note: dimity is a light ribbed cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A cotton fabric that has been turned and cut is now shrinking in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing DIMITY gives YTIMID; 'shortened' drops the last letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking person is shy and retiring, a synonym for fearful in company.

clue.text: Welsh chief to extend credit through local peninsula

indicators.note: the lending runs through the middle of the peninsula's name

parts.note: Gower is a peninsula in south Wales, local to a Welsh chief
to lend is to extend credit

explanation.surface: A Welsh leader lending money across his own corner of the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gower is a peninsula near Swansea in Wales; 'local' ties it to the Welsh chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndŵr, anglicised Glendower, led a Welsh revolt against English rule around 1400.

clue.text: Smug politician given chair speaking

parts.note: CON is short for a Conservative politician

indicators.note: the words are said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: someone given a chair is seated

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied MP who has been handed a seat, perhaps on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' says SEATED is heard, spelt CEITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain and self-satisfied, so smug.

clue.text: Fish heading away from seaweed

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, leaves the seaweed word

parts.note: tangle is a name for kelp-type seaweed

explanation.surface: A fish swimming away from the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Flower in dry earth finally lost

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter is lost from the word

parts.note: dust is dry, powdery earth

explanation.surface: A flower lost in parched soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows; the Indus runs through Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a river, and a river is a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Not entirely chicken, working for classic tourist attraction

parts.note: part, as in partly, means not entirely
a hen is a female chicken
on means working, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A partly chicken creature working at a famous sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon in Athens is a classical Greek temple visited by many tourists.

clue.text: In protective gear, doctor loves to probe intestine

indicators.note: the doctor and loves push inside the intestine

parts.note: the gut is the intestine
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
love is zero in tennis, so loves are two Os

explanation.surface: A doctor in a protective suit examining a patient's bowel.
explanation.walkthrough: A gumboot is a rubber wellington boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboot is a rubber boot worn to keep feet dry, so protective clothing.

clue.text: Headband as relic demolished in court

indicators.note: the shuffled relic goes inside the court abbreviation
the relic is knocked down and rebuilt, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiara exhibited as an old relic was destroyed during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges the relic into IRCLE, and 'in' sets those letters inside the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A circlet is a small circular band worn on the head, a type of headband.

clue.text: Make small error at end of simple knot

parts.note: to nod is to make a slip through inattention, as in 'Homer nods'

indicators.note: the last letter of the word simple is taken

explanation.surface: A slip made at the finish of tying a basic knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knob or knot, as on a plant stem or in a swelling.

clue.text: 'Go for gold' — our team brochure

parts.note: to prospect is to search for gold
us means our side, our team

explanation.surface: A sporting team's motivational slogan printed in its publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospectus is a printed booklet describing a school, company or offer, a kind of brochure.

clue.text: Suspect professor bowled a heavy ball

parts.note: Professor Plum is one of the suspects in the board game Cluedo
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A suspicious academic delivers a heavy ball at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo (Clue in North America) is a murder-mystery board game whose suspects include Professor Plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb is the lead weight on a plumb line, a heavy ball or bob.

clue.text: Officer that may be sleeping in the street

definitions.text: Officer that may be sleeping in the street

parts.words: Officer that may be sleeping in the street
parts.note: the surface pictures a dozing constable on the beat

explanation.surface: A constable dozing on duty in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'sleeping policeman' is a speed bump.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the law is a constable, and the speed-bump idiom makes one lie in the road.

clue.text: Good book suggesting vin rosé?

parts.note: the letters of version rearranged make vin rose, so the wine is a reworked version of that word

explanation.surface: A wine guide recommending pink wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the two words as wordplay: an anagram indicator plus VERSION gives VIN ROSE. The Revised Version is an 1880s English Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Good Book is the Bible, and the Revised Version is one English translation of it.

clue.text: Fieldwork is hard, progressing slowly

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
edging means moving forward bit by bit

explanation.surface: Research out in the field is tough going and slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedging, the planting and laying of hedges, is literally work done on fields.

clue.text: Westminster unknowns taking heart to allege fraud

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode of Westminster, read with the 1 as I
Z is a mathematical unknown, so two are ZZ

indicators.note: the central letters of the word allege are taken

explanation.surface: Anonymous figures in Parliament at the core of a fraud allegation.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the postcode for Westminster, home of the UK Parliament; the digit 1 serves as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swizzle is British slang for a swindle or let-down, a variant of swizz.

clue.text: Sign to get up, having succeeded getting down

indicators.note: in this down clue the letter goes lower, to the bottom of the word

parts.note: to arise is to get up
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An astrological portent telling you to rise, though you then got down.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of ARISE drops to the end, giving ARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: PM's end historically comes in short scuffle

indicators.note: the archaic word for an end enters the shortened scuffle
the scuffle loses its last letter

parts.note: a melee is a confused fight or scuffle
bourn is an archaic word for a goal or boundary, an end

explanation.surface: A prime minister's downfall long ago came in a brief brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the scuffle to MELE; the old word for an end is familiar from Hamlet's 'undiscovered country from whose bourn no traveller returns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Melbourne was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and mentor to Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Plug vainly away at course involving lashings of meat?

definitions.meaning: to keep pressing a cause that is already lost
a meal course in which horse meat, already dead, gets whipped: lashings means both plenty and blows

explanation.surface: Persisting hopelessly with a dish served in generous helpings of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading pictures literal flogging of a dead horse served as a dinner course; 'lashings' is a pun on whipping and plentiful amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means wasting effort on a matter already settled or beyond hope.

clue.text: Eating heartily, and settling for the night?

definitions.meaning: eating with enthusiasm, as in getting stuck into a meal
making someone snug in bed by folding the bedclothes around them

explanation.surface: A hearty dinner and then bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has both senses: devouring food greedily and wrapping a child up in bed.

clue.text: Sleepers keep moving about, finally peaceful in rest

parts.note: to wag on is to go on wagging, moving to and fro

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the word for rest

parts.note: to sit is to rest

indicators.note: the last letter of peaceful is taken

explanation.surface: People asleep keep shifting about, and only at last lie quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepers' misleads as people or railway ties; here it means sleeping cars on European trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons-lits are railway sleeping cars, the French term used across continental Europe.

clue.text: Who to go to for better advice?

definitions.text: Who to go to for better advice?

parts.words: Who to go to for better advice?
parts.note: the surface asks for improved counsel, but a better is one who bets

explanation.surface: A question about whom to consult for sounder guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective; it is a noun, someone placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells or gives forecasts on races to punters, offering advice to gamblers.

clue.text: In dreadful cold, put over extremely short works in theatre

parts.note: dire means dreadful
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something over turns it upside down, so the letters are reversed
the outermost letters of the word short are taken

explanation.surface: In a terrible chill, someone stages very brief theatrical pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'short' give ST, and 'put over' turns them to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre director stages plays, so someone who directs works in theatre.

clue.text: Like St Paul's work by sea

parts.note: to do is to work or perform
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A description of the cathedral as a construction beside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its great dome, so it is domed.

clue.text: For dissection, sent a part of body

indicators.note: the words are cut up and reassembled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specimen delivered to an anatomy lab for students to cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical term for the buttocks, a part of the body.
